chapter: Fats Pichon and the steamer Capitol
title: Practicing on the boat and why he practiced solos
summary: He seldom practiced alone; when he did, he worked on new solo ideas because soloing was how musicians were rated.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: I don't know where I got a glass.
Well, I mean, did you practice on your own as well? A part of the band practice?
Very seldom. Very seldom. I mean, I...
Yeah, always was with the band. You see, at some time, or rather on a boat, maybe some guys would feel like practicing. You understand? So, uh...
Huh? I want to... Give me about a half a glass or something. When you did practice by yourself, what did you practice? Scales or long notes?

No. No, I didn't practice no scales. I didn't practice no long notes or nothing. I mean, I used to practice to play more, you know. I mean, to play more solos. Yeah. Because, uh, uh, solos were the thing at that time, you know. See? To play the solos, you know. See? So, in other words, I mean, that's how you were rated with the public. Yeah, that's good. That's how you was rated with the public is with the solos, you know. That's it. Of course, I mean, well, at that time, I mean, I was... I could read like that, you know. So, I mean, I probably wasn't reading anymore. See? My problem was when I do practice, I mean, practice some new ideas or something in solo way. See? So, some of the guys used to play, uh, used to practice their horn like that on a boat when the boat be going from town to town. So, uh, well, then some of the deckhands on the boat and all that, they be, some of them be resting or so like that, and then they complain to the captain about them boys, just to have them. Oh, no, we're getting a chance. Yeah, yeah.
